{{Short description|Hungarian physicist}}
{{Western name order|Bergou János}}

'''János Bergou''' (born 22 March 1947) is a Hungarian physicist and academic who is currently a professor at [[Hunter College]] in New York. In 2009, he was awarded the status of Fellow in the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref> after they were nominated by their Division of Laser Science in 2009,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2009&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellows 2009|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref> for "outstanding work in quantum optics and quantum information, in particular work on the theory of correlated emission lasers, the effect of pump statistics on the nature of the electromagnetic field produced in lasers and micromasers, and on quantum state discrimination."

Bergou earned a master's in science (1970) and earned his PhD ''summa cum laude'' in Theoretical Physics (1975) from [[Eötvös Loránd University]] in Budapest.<ref>{{cite news|title=Munkatársak - Dr. Bergou János {{!}} PTE TTK FI|url=http://www.physics.ttk.pte.hu/munkatarsak/bergou|accessdate=23 August 2017|publisher=University of Pécs Faculty of Science Physics Institute|language=hu}}</ref> From the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]], he received his [[Habilitation]] (CSc) (1982) and Doctor of Sciences (DSc) (1994).<ref>{{cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae —János Bergou|url=http://www.hunter.cuny.edu/physics/faculty/bergou/curriculum-vitae|website=www.hunter.cuny.edu|publisher=Hunter College|accessdate=23 August 2017|language=en}}</ref>
